competitor_reference.title: The only SAT Math Desmos Guide you'll ever need

modules.title: Systems of Linear Equations: The 5-Second Intersection Trick
modules.problem_statement: If 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x - y = 9, what is the value of x + y?
modules.algebra_trap: Manual elimination/substitution takes 90 seconds with high risk of minus-sign arithmetic errors.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Type both equations exactly as written. Click the gray dot at the intersection (2, 5). Add 2 + 5 = 7 directly in Desmos in under 5 seconds.
modules.pro_tip: If the SAT asks for x - y or 2x + 3y, never solve by hand—just grab the intersection coordinates and type the target expression into Desmos line 3.

modules.title: Quadratic Vertices, Maximums, Minimums & Roots
modules.problem_statement: A projectile's height is given by h(t) = -16t^2 + 64t + 80. At what time t does it reach maximum height, and what is the maximum height?
modules.algebra_trap: Using vertex formula -b/(2a) and plugging back in takes 2 minutes and invites sign errors.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Type y = -16x^2 + 64x + 80. Click the peak gray dot at the vertex (2, 144). Answer: t = 2 seconds, max height = 144 feet.
modules.pro_tip: Desmos automatically highlights roots (x-intercepts), y-intercept, and the vertex with clickable gray dots. One click reveals all key points.

modules.title: The Ultimate Regression Cheat Code (Table to Equation)
modules.problem_statement: Given points (1, 5), (2, 11), and (3, 19), which quadratic function f(x) models this data?
modules.algebra_trap: Setting up a 3-variable system (a + b + c = 5, etc.) takes 3-4 minutes and is heavily error-prone.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Add a table with x1 and y1. In the next line type: y1 ~ ax1^2 + bx1 + c. Desmos instantly calculates a = 1, b = 3, c = 1. Equation is f(x) = x^2 + 3x + 1.
modules.pro_tip: The tilde symbol (~) tells Desmos to run an instant regression. Works for linear (y1 ~ mx1 + b), quadratic, and exponential (y1 ~ a*b^x1).

modules.title: Unknown Constant k: Infinite Solutions & No Solution
modules.problem_statement: For what value of k does the system 4x + 6y = 12 and 2x + ky = 7 have no solution?
modules.algebra_trap: Cross-multiplying coefficients or setting slopes equal can confuse students on whether intercepts match.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Type line 1: 4x + 6y = 12. Type line 2: 2x + ky = 7. Click 'add slider k'. Slide k until the lines are perfectly parallel (slope matched at k = 3).
modules.pro_tip: Parallel lines = No solution. Overlapping lines = Infinite solutions. The Desmos slider makes abstract constant problems purely visual.

modules.title: Circle Equations, Centers & Radii in 10 Seconds
modules.problem_statement: The equation of a circle is x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 8y = 24. What is the radius of the circle?
modules.algebra_trap: Completing the square twice (adding 9 and 16) is a classic trap where students drop negative signs.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Type x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 8y = 24 into Desmos. Look at the circle. The center is at (3, -4). The rightmost point is (10, -4). Distance from 3 to 10 is 7. Radius = 7.
modules.pro_tip: Desmos graphs circles even in general form. No completing the square required on the Digital SAT.

modules.title: Systems of Inequalities & Shaded Feasible Regions
modules.problem_statement: Which of the following points (x, y) is in the solution set of y >= 2x - 3 and y < -x + 5? A) (0, 6) B) (2, 2) C) (4, 1) D) (-1, 8)
modules.algebra_trap: Plugging 4 answer choices into two inequalities takes 8 individual algebra evaluations.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Type y >= 2x - 3 and y < -x + 5. Desmos shades the overlap in dark purple. Plot the 4 points. Only (2, 2) lies inside the shaded overlap and not on a dashed line.
modules.pro_tip: Desmos automatically distinguishes solid lines (>=, <=) from dashed lines (>, <). Points on dashed boundary lines are never valid solutions.

modules.title: Function Notation f(x) and Function Transformations
modules.problem_statement: If f(x) = 3x^2 - 5x + 4, what is the value of f(a + 2) - f(a) when a = 3?
modules.algebra_trap: Expanding 3(a+2)^2 - 5(a+2) + 4 and subtracting f(a) algebraically takes 2 pages of scrap paper.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Line 1: f(x) = 3x^2 - 5x + 4. Line 2: a = 3. Line 3: f(a + 2) - f(a). Desmos outputs the exact numeric answer 46 instantly.
modules.pro_tip: Desmos supports full functional evaluation. You can define f(x), g(x), and evaluate nested expressions like f(g(2)) in 1 line.

modules.title: Exponential Growth, Decay & Percentage Multipliers
modules.problem_statement: A population of bacteria grows by 15% every 3 hours. If the initial count is 500, which equation models population P after t hours?
modules.algebra_trap: Confusing annual vs hourly growth and placing t/3 vs 3t in the exponent.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Type target values for t = 3: P should be 500 * 1.15 = 575. Graph the 4 options: P = 500(1.15)^(t/3) passes through (3, 575). Instant match.
modules.pro_tip: When in doubt on exponent models, plug in t = 0 and t = period, then visually check which graph hits the exact coordinates.

modules.title: SAT Statistics in 3 Clicks: Mean, Median & Box Plots
modules.problem_statement: Given the dataset: 14, 18, 22, 22, 25, 29, 31, 35, 42. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
modules.algebra_trap: Ordering numbers manually, finding Q1 and Q3, and doing subtraction by hand leads to silly arithmetic misses.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Line 1: L = [14, 18, 22, 22, 25, 29, 31, 35, 42]. Line 2: stats(L). Desmos prints Min, Q1, Median, Q3, Max in a clean table. IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 33 - 20 = 13 (or q3(L) - q1(L)).
modules.pro_tip: Desmos has built-in statistical functions: mean(L), median(L), stdev(L), and boxplot(L). Never compute summary stats by hand.

modules.title: Hard Geometry & Trig on Desmos + 800-Score Checklist
modules.problem_statement: In right triangle ABC, angle C is 90 deg, and sin(A) = 5/13. What is cos(90 - A) and tan(B)?
modules.algebra_trap: Trying to memorize complementary angle identities under test anxiety.
modules.desmos_cheat_code: Switch Desmos to DEGREE mode (wrench icon). Line 1: A = arcsin(5/13). Line 2: cos(90 - A) = 0.3846 (equals 5/13). Line 3: B = 90 - A; tan(B) = 2.4 (12/5).
modules.pro_tip: Always ensure the Wrench settings match Degrees vs Radians. Desmos evaluates arcsin, arccos, and full right-triangle geometry.
